boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 4 features for Kansas, measured 2026-11-12. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 4 districts (every intersection-over-union 1.0), so nothing changes on 3 January 2027, and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

TIGERweb's secondary and elementary layers carry nothing for Kansas, so they are not drawn.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 710 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that reach into Kansas (890 in the app's bounding box), drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs that reach into Kansas (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='20'. The app's box reaches into Nebraska, Missouri, Oklahoma and Colorado, and measured 2026-11-12, 710 of the 890 ZCTAs in it reach into Kansas and are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Kansas. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City
layers.rank_note: 626 incorporated cities, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 626 records: 623 active cities, the city of Frederick, which the Census records as an inactive government, the city of Tribune, which it records as having no functioning government, and the balance of Greeley County's unified government, measured 2026-11-12. MOST OF KANSAS IS IN NO INCORPORATED CITY (about 3% of its land, 6,203.9 of 211,754.3 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. Kansas City and Wyandotte County are one government, the Unified Government; the Census records Tribune as having no functioning government of its own, because the city and Greeley County are one unified government, which it also draws as a place; each card says which. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Kansas's mayors and councils was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap ks-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-12: 407 points in Kansas's envelope, which reaches into Nebraska, Missouri, Oklahoma and Colorado; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages if that is ever reached.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Kansas — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Kansas State Capitol, 300 SW 10th Avenue, Topeka, Shawnee County

negative_point.note: Webster County, Nebraska, about 20 km north of the Kansas line — outside Kansas and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-12: TIGERweb's state layer names Nebraska here (control: the State Capitol returns Kansas), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does, nor any of the other batch-3 states' outlines. A POINT ON A NEIGHBOUR'S LAND MOVES THE DAY THAT NEIGHBOUR GOES LIVE: Nebraska is in batch 4 of the state-level launch, and the change that makes it live moves this point. Every other neighbour of Kansas is live or goes live in batch 3.

geometry.note: The whole-Kansas outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (105 counties).
Kansas's 105 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 4 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the same map as layer 4 (CD119).
The 40 Kansas Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper).
The 125 Kansas House districts, TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower).

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Kansas elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from ks/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
